            tathā coktam --- sa khalv ayaṃ brāhmaṇo yathā yathā vratāni bahūni samāditsate tathā
            tathā pramādakṛtebhyo hiṃsānidānebhyo nivartamānas tām evāvadātarūpām ahiṃsāṃ karoti.
children.translated_text: There, <s>ahiṃsā</s> is the non-harming of all beings in every way, at all times. And the subsequent restraints and observances (<s>yama</s> and <s>niyama</s>) have this as their root, since they are aimed at the accomplishment of this, they are taught in order to establish this; they are adopted precisely to fashion this bright-clear form. Thus it is said—“This Brāhmaṇa, in proportion as he desires to undertake many vows, turning back from negligences that cause himsa (injury) and from sources of injury, makes <s>ahiṃsā</s> of that very bright-clear form.”

children.text:
satyaṃ yathārthe vāṅmanase. yathā dṛṣṭaṃ yathānumitaṃ tathā vāṅ manaś ceti. paratra
            svabodhasaṃkrāntaye vāg uktā, sā yadi na vañcitā bhrāntā vā pratipattivandhyā vā bhaved
            iti. eṣā sarvabhūtopakārārthaṃ pravṛttā na bhūtopaghātāya. yadi caivam apy abhidhīyamānā
            bhūtopaghātaparaiva syān na satyaṃ bhavet pāpam eva bhavet tena puṇyābhāsena
            puṇyapratirūpakeṇa kaṣṭaṃ tamaḥ prāpnuyāt. tasmāt parīkṣya sarvabhūtahitaṃ satyaṃ
            brūyāt.
children.translated_text: Truth (<s>satya</s>) is speech and mind in accordance with what is real: as seen, as inferred, so are speech and mind. Speech is enjoined elsewhere for the transmission of one’s own understanding; if that should be deceitful, deluded, or barren of apprehension, then [it fails]. This is undertaken for the welfare of all beings, not for the harm of beings. And if, even so, what is spoken should be intent on the harm of beings, it would not be truth; it would be sin indeed, and by that semblance of merit, a counterfeit of merit, one would attain a grievous darkness. Therefore, having examined, one should speak truth that is for the good of all beings

children.text:
steyam aśāstrapūrvakaṃ dravyāṇāṃ parataḥ svīkaraṇaṃ, tatpratiṣedhaḥ punar aspṛhārūpam
            asteyam iti. brahmacaryaṃ guptendriyasyopasthasya saṃyamaḥ. viṣayāṇām
            arjanarakṣaṇakṣayasaṅgahiṃsādoṣadarśanād asvīkaraṇam aparigraha ity ete yamāḥ.
children.translated_text: Non-stealing (<s>asteya</s>) is the taking of others’ property without scriptural warrant; its prohibition, again, is the form of non-covetousness—thus it is <s>asteya</s>. <s>Brahmacarya</s> is the restraint of the generative organ for one whose senses are guarded. From perceiving the faults of acquisition, protection, loss, attachment, and injury with respect to objects, not accepting—this is <s>aparigraha</s>. These are the restraints (<s>yamāḥ</s>)
As for these—
Not delimited by class, place, time, or occasion—they are universal, the great vow

children.text:
tatrāhiṃsā jātyavacchinnā matsyavadhakasya matsyeṣv eva nānyatra hiṃsā. saiva
            deśāvacchinnā na tīrthe haniṣyāmīti. saiva kālāvacchinnā na caturdaśyāṃ na puṇye+ahani
            haniṣyāmīti. saiva tribhir uparatasya samayāvacchinnā devabrāhmaṇārthe nānyathā
            haniṣyāmīti. yathā ca kṣatriyāṇāṃ yuddha eva hiṃsā nānyatreti. ebhir
            jātideśakālasamayair anavacchinnā ahiṃsādayaḥ sarvathaiva paripālanīyāḥ. sarvabhūmiṣu
            sarvaviṣayeṣu sarvathaivāviditavyabhicārāḥ sārvabhaumā mahāvratam ity ucyante.
children.translated_text: There, <s>ahiṃsā</s> delimited by class is, for a fisherman, only with regard to fish and not otherwise injury; the same delimited by place is, “I will not kill at a sacred ford”; the same delimited by time is, “Not on the fourteenth, not on an auspicious day will I kill”; the same delimited by convention for one who has refrained by these three is, “For the sake of gods or Brāhmaṇas, and not otherwise, will I kill.” And as for Kṣatriyas, injury is only in battle and not otherwise. But not delimited by these—class, place, time, and convention—<s>ahiṃsā</s> and the rest are to be observed absolutely in every way. Because they are to be known as without any transgression anywhere, in all domains and in every way, they are called universal, the great vow

Purity (<s>śauca</s>), contentment (<s>saṃtoṣa</s>), austerity (<s>tapas</s>), recitation-and-study (<s>svādhyāya</s>), and dedication to the Lord (<s>īśvara-praṇidhāna</s>) are the observances (<s>niyamāḥ</s>)

children.text:
tatra śaucaṃ mṛjjalādijanitaṃ medhyābhyavaharaṇādi ca bāhyam. ābhyantaraṃ cittamalānām
            ākṣālanam. saṃtoṣaḥ saṃnihitasādhanād adhikasyānupāditsā. tapo dvaṃdvasahanam. dvaṃdvāś
            ca jighatsāpipāse śītoṣṇe sthānāsane kāṣṭhamaunākāramaune ca. vratāni caiṣāṃ yathāyogaṃ
            kṛcchracāndrāyaṇasāṃtapanādīni. svādhyāyo mokṣaśāstrāṇām adhyayanaṃ praṇavajapo vā.
            īśvarapraṇidhānaṃ tasmin paramagurau sarvakarmārpaṇam.
children.translated_text: There, purity (<s>śauca</s>) external is produced by rubbing with water and the like, and includes the taking of what is clean (pure) as food, and so on; internal is the washing away of the stains of the mind (<s>citta</s>). Contentment (<s>saṃtoṣa</s>) is the non-coveting of what is beyond the means at hand. Austerity (<s>tapas</s>) is the endurance of the pairs of opposites; and the pairs are hunger and thirst, cold and heat, standing and sitting, the wooden-vow silence and the form-vow silence. And the vows for these, according to fitness, are the <s>kṛcchra</s>, <s>cāndrāyaṇa</s>, <s>sāṃtapana</s>, and the like. Recitation-and-study (<s>svādhyāya</s>) is the study of the scriptures concerning liberation, or else the muttered repetition of the <s>praṇava</s> (om). Dedication to the Lord (<s>īśvara-praṇidhāna</s>) is the offering of all actions unto Him, the supreme teacher

children.text: śayyāsanastho+atha pathi vrajan vā svasthaḥ parikṣīṇavitarkajālaḥ /
children.translated_text: Lying on a bed, or seated, or then traveling on a path, or being at ease in oneself, one whose net of deliberations has been worn away,
beholding the exhaustion of the seed of transmigration (<s>saṃsāra</s>), would be constantly yoked (steadfast), a partaker of the enjoyment of the deathless (nectar)

children.text: yatredam uktaṃ tataḥ pratyakcetanādhigamo+apy antarāyābhāvaś ceti.
children.translated_text: Where this has been said: from that there is also the attainment of inward-turned consciousness (<s>pratyak-cetanā</s>), and the absence of obstacles
For these restraints and observances (<s>yama</s> and <s>niyama</s>)—
When there is disturbance by contrary deliberations (<s>vitarka</s>), there is the cultivation of the opposite (counter-reflection) (<s>pratipakṣa-bhāvanā</s>)

children.text:
yadāsya brāhmaṇasya hiṃsādayo vitarkā jāyeran haniṣyāmy aham apakāriṇam anṛtam api
            vakṣyāmi dravyam apy asya svīkariṣyāmi dāreṣu cāsya vyavāyī bhaviṣyāmi parigraheṣu cāsya
            svāmī bhaviṣyāmīti. evam unmārgapravaṇavitarkajvareṇātidīptena bādhyamānas
            tatpratipakṣān bhāvayet. ghoreṣu saṃsārāṅgāreṣu pacyamānena mayā śaraṇam upāgataḥ
            sarvabhūtābhayapradānena yogadharmaḥ. sa khalv ahaṃ tyaktvā vitarkān punas tān ādadānas
            tulyaḥ śvavṛtteneti bhāvayet. yathā śvā vāntāvalehī tathā tyaktasya punar ādadāna iti.
            evamādi sūtrāntareṣv api yojyam.
children.translated_text: When, for this Brāhmaṇa, deliberations such as injury arise—“I shall kill the wrongdoer; I shall even speak falsehood; I shall take even his property; and with respect to his wives I shall engage in intercourse; and with respect to his possessions I shall become the master”—thus, being afflicted by the fever of deliberations that are bent on a wrong path, blazing exceedingly, he should cultivate their opposites. “I, being cooked in the terrible embers of <s>saṃsāra</s>, have taken refuge: by granting fearlessness to all beings is the <s>yoga</s>-duty.” And, “I indeed, having abandoned deliberations, if I again take them up, am like one of a dog’s behavior”—so let him reflect; “Just as a dog licks up its vomit, so is the taking up again of what has been abandoned.” The like should be applied also in other sūtra-passages

children.text:
vitarkā hiṃsādayaḥ kṛtakāritānumoditā lobhakrodhamohapūrvakā mṛdumadhyādhimātrā
              duḥkhājñānānantaphalā iti pratipakṣabhāvanam
children.translated_text: Deliberations—injury and the rest—done, caused to be done, or approved, preceded by greed, anger, and delusion, mild, middling, or intense, have suffering, ignorance, and endlessness as their fruit—this is the counter-reflection (<s>pratipakṣa-bhāvanā</s>)

children.text:
tatra hiṃsā tāvat --- kṛtā kāritānumoditeti tridhā. ekaikā punas tridhā lobhena
            māṃsacarmārthena krodhenāpakṛtam aneneti mohena dharmo me bhaviṣyatīti. lobhakrodhamohāḥ
            punas trividhā mṛdumadhyādhimātrā iti. evaṃ saptaviṃśatir bhedā bhavanti hiṃsāyāḥ.
            mṛdumadhyādhimātrāḥ punas tridhā --- mṛdumṛdur madhyamṛdus tīvramṛdur iti. tathā
            mṛdumadhyo madhyamadhyas tīvramadhya iti. tathā mṛdutīvro madhyatīvro+adhimātratīvra
            iti. evam ekāśītibhedā hiṃsā bhavati. sā punar niyamavikalpasamuccayabhedād asaṃkhyeyā,
            prāṇabhṛdbhedasyāparisaṃkhyeyatvād iti. evam anṛtādiṣv api yojyam.

children.translated_text: Indeed, those deliberations have suffering, ignorance, and endlessness as their fruit—this is the counter-reflection: those whose fruit is suffering, ignorance, and endlessness. And thus, the injurer, to begin with, strikes down the strength of the one to be slain; then, by the fall of weapon and the like, he causes suffering; then he releases him even from life. Then, because of that striking down of strength, the sentient and insentient instruments of the injurer become of diminished vigor. Producing suffering, he experiences suffering in hell, animal, ghost, and the like; and, because he has removed another’s opportunity for living, at every moment, being in the vicinity of the end of life, wishing even for death, he barely draws breath, since the experiencing of the ripening of suffering is bound to its fixed ripening. And if, by some means, injury be attended by the fading of merit, then, upon the attainment of pleasure there, he would be of short life—thus. The same is to be applied, as possible, also to falsehood and the rest. children.translated_text: and he who is not negligent, through yoga, delights in yoga for a long time

The application of that <s>saṃyama</s> is upon the stage immediately following the stage that has been mastered; for one who has not mastered the lower stage does not, leaping over the immediately subsequent stage, obtain <s>saṃyama</s> on the farthest stages; and in the absence of that, whence would there be his illumination of insight? By the grace of the Lord (<s>īśvara</s>), however, for one who has mastered the higher stages, <s>saṃyama</s> on the lower stages—such as knowledge of another’s mind—is appropriate; why? Because the purpose of that is known from elsewhere. “This is the stage immediately following that stage”—in this matter, yoga itself is the instructor. How so? For it has been said, “
The triad is more internal than the previous [five]

children.text:
tad etad dhāraṇādhyānasamādhitrayam antaraṅgaṃ saṃprajñātasya samādheḥ pūrvebhyo
            yamādibhyaḥ pañcabhyaḥ sādhanebhya iti.
children.translated_text: This very triad of <s>dhāraṇā</s>, <s>dhyāna</s>, and <s>samādhi</s> is inner with respect to the cognitive absorption with discernment (<s>saṃprajñāta-samādhi</s>), compared to the previous five practices beginning with the restraints (<s>yama</s>)
Yet that too is external with respect to the seedless [absorption]

children.text:
tad apy antaraṅgaṃ sādhanatrayaṃ nirbījasya yogasya bahiraṅgaṃ bhavati kasmāt,
            tadabhāve bhāvād iti.
children.translated_text: Even that inner triad of practices becomes external with respect to the seedless yoga (<s>nirbīja</s>), because in its absence [i.e., when that triad is absent], [seedless] occurs—thus

children.text: atha nirodhacittakṣaṇeṣu calaṃ guṇavṛttam iti kīdṛśas tadā cittapariṇāmaḥ ---
children.translated_text: Now, at the moments when the mind is in restraint (<s>nirodha</s>), the activity of the <s>guṇa</s>-s is unsteady—what, then, is the transformation of the mind at that time?—

The overpowering and arising of the impressions (saṃskāra) of emergence and restraint, together with the mind at the moment of restraint—this is the transformation into restraint (<s>nirodha-pariṇāma</s>)

children.text:
vyutthānasaṃskārāś cittadharmā na te pratyayātmakā iti pratyayanirodhe na niruddhā
            nirodhasaṃskārā api cittadharmās tayor abhibhavaprādurbhāvau vyutthānasaṃskārā hīyante
            nirodhasaṃskārā ādhīyante. nirodhakṣaṇaṃ cittam anveti tad ekasya cittasya pratikṣaṇam
            idaṃ saṃskārānyathātvaṃ nirodhapariṇāmaḥ. tadā saṃskāraśeṣaṃ cittam iti nirodhasamādhau
            vyākhyātam.
children.translated_text: The impressions of emergence (<s>vyutthāna-saṃskāra</s>) are properties of the mind, and they are not of the form of a cognitive content; therefore, when the cognitive contents are restrained, they are not restrained [i.e., they remain as impressions]. The impressions of restraint (<s>nirodha-saṃskāra</s>) also are properties of the mind; of these two there are overpowering and arising: the emergence-impressions wane, the restraint-impressions are increased. The mind adheres to the moment of restraint; this per-moment alteration of impressions in one and the same mind is the transformation into restraint. Then it is a mind with impressions remaining—so it has been explained in restraint-absorption (<s>nirodha-samādhi</s>)
Its flow toward peacefulness is due to impression (saṃskāra)

children.text:
nirodhasaṃskārābhyāsapāṭavāpekṣā praśāntavāhitā cittasya bhavati. tatsaṃskāramāndye
            vyutthānadharmiṇā saṃskāreṇa nirodhadharmasaṃskāro+abhibhūyata iti.
children.translated_text: The flow of the mind toward peace occurs in dependence upon skill in the practice of the restraint-impressions; when that impression is weak, the impression having the nature of emergence overcomes the restraint-natured impression

The subsidence and arising of [respectively] all-objectedness (<s>sarvārthatā</s>) and one-pointedness (<s>ekāgratā</s>) of the mind—this is the transformation into absorption (<s>samādhi-pariṇāma</s>)

children.text:
sarvārthatā cittadharmaḥ. ekāgratāpi cittadharmaḥ. sarvārthatāyāḥ kṣayas tirobhāva ity
            arthaḥ. ekāgratāyā udaya āvirbhāva ity arthaḥ. tayor dharmitvenānugataṃ cittaṃ, tad idaṃ
            cittam apāyopajanayoḥ svātmabhūtayor dharmayor anugataṃ samādhīyate sa cittasya
            samādhipariṇāmaḥ.
children.translated_text: All-objectedness (<s>sarvārthatā</s>) is a property of the mind (<s>citta</s), one-pointedness (<s>ekāgratā</s>) too is a property of the mind; the subsidence of all-objectedness is its disappearance—this is the meaning, the arising of one-pointedness is its manifestation—this is the meaning; the mind, accompanied by these two as its properties (dharma) by being their substrate (dharmitva), that very mind, accompanied by the two properties which are its own nature, namely disappearance and arising, is brought into absorption—this is the transformation of the mind into absorption (<s>samādhi-pariṇāma</s>)
From that, then, again,
The mind’s transformation into one-pointedness (<s>ekāgratā-pariṇāma</s>) is [that state in which] the quieted and the arisen [cognitive contents] are of equal content

children.text:
samāhitacittasya pūrvapratyayaḥ śānta uttaras tatsadṛśa uditaḥ, samādhicittam ubhayor
            anugataṃ punas tathaivāsamādhibhreṣād iti. sa khalv ayaṃ dharmiṇaś
            cittasyaikāgratāpariṇāmaḥ.
children.translated_text: For a mind established in absorption (<s>samāhita-citta</s>), the prior cognitive content is quieted, the subsequent one, similar to that, is arisen; the mind-in-samādhi, being accompanied by both, again just so, is not confused by non-samādhi; this indeed is the transformation into one-pointedness of the substrate that is the mind
By this, the transformations of property (dharma), mark (lakṣaṇa), and state (avasthā) with respect to elements and senses (<s>bhūta</s>-s and <s>indriya</s>-s) have been explained

children.text:
etena pūrvoktena cittapariṇāmena dharmalakṣaṇāvasthārūpeṇa bhūtendriyeṣu dharmapariṇāmo
            lakṣaṇapariṇāmo+avasthāpariṇāmaś cokto veditavyaḥ. tatra vyutthānanirodhayor
            abhibhavaprādurbhāvau dharmiṇi dharmapariṇāmaḥ. lakṣaṇapariṇāmaś ca nirodhas trilakṣaṇas
            tribhir adhvabhir yuktaḥ. sa khalv anāgatalakṣaṇam adhvānaṃ prathamaṃ hitvā dharmatvam
            anatikrānto vartamānalakṣaṇaṃ pratipannaḥ. yatrāsya svarūpeṇābhivyaktiḥ. eṣo+asya
            dvitīyo+adhvā. na cātītānāgatābhyāṃ lakṣaṇābhyāṃ viyuktaḥ.
children.translated_text: By this previously stated transformation of the mind, which is of the form of property, mark, and state, one should understand that in the <s>bhūta</s>-s and <s>indriya</s>-s there are the property-transformation, the mark-transformation, and the state-transformation; therein, the overpowering and manifestation of emergence and restraint, occurring in the substrate (dharman), is the property-transformation; and the mark-transformation is restraint, which is three-marked and joined with the three time-tracks (adhvan-s); it, having first left behind the future-marked track, does not overstep its own property, and attains the present-mark; where there is manifestation in its own form—this is its second track; nor is it dissociated from the marks of past and future

children.text:
tathā vyutthānaṃ trilakṣaṇaṃ tribhir adhvabhir yuktaṃ vartamānalakṣaṇaṃ hitvā
            dharmatvam anatikrāntam atītalakṣaṇaṃ pratipannam. eṣo+asya tṛtīyo+adhvā. na
            cānāgatavartamānābhyāṃ lakṣaṇābhyāṃ viyuktam. evaṃ punar vyutthānam upasaṃpadyamānam
            anāgatalakṣaṇaṃ hitvā dharmatvam anatikrāntaṃ vartamānalakṣaṇaṃ pratipannam. yatrāsya
            svarūpābhivyaktau satyāṃ vyāpāraḥ eṣo+asya dvitīyo+adhvā. na cātītānāgatābhyāṃ
            lakṣaṇābhyāṃ viyuktam iti. evaṃ punar nirodha evaṃ punar vyutthānam iti.
children.translated_text: Likewise emergence is three-marked and joined with the three time-tracks; having left the present-mark, not overstepping its own property, it attains the past-mark—this is its third track; nor is it dissociated from the marks of future and present; thus again, emergence, as it is being attained, having left the future-mark, not overstepping its own property, attains the present-mark; where, when there is manifestation of its own nature, there is operation—this is its second track; nor is it dissociated from the marks of past and future—thus; thus again [there is] restraint, thus again [there is] emergence

children.text:
tathāvasthāpariṇāmaḥ tatra nirodhakṣaṇeṣu nirodhasaṃskārā balavanto bhavanti durbalā
            vyutthānasaṃskārā iti. eṣa dharmāṇām avasthāpariṇāmaḥ. tatra dharmiṇo dharmaiḥ pariṇāmo
            dharmāṇāṃ tryadhvanāṃ lakṣaṇaiḥ pariṇāmo lakṣaṇānām apy avasthābhiḥ pariṇāma iti. evaṃ
            dharmalakṣaṇāvasthāpariṇāmaiḥ śūnyaṃ na kṣaṇam api guṇavṛttam avatiṣṭhate. calaṃ ca
            guṇavṛttam. guṇasvābhāvyaṃ tu pravṛttikāraṇam uktaṃ guṇānām iti. etena bhūtendriyeṣu
            dharmadharmibhedāt trividhaḥ pariṇāmo veditavyaḥ.
children.translated_text: So also the state-transformation: there, at the moments of restraint, the impressions of restraint (<s>nirodha-saṃskāra</s>) become strong, the impressions of emergence (<s>vyutthāna-saṃskāra</s>) weak—thus; this is the state-transformation of properties; therein, there is transformation of the substrate by the properties, transformation of the properties by the marks of the three tracks, and transformation of the marks too by the states; thus, by the transformations of property, mark, and state, not even for a moment does the activity of the <s>guṇa</s>-s remain empty; and the activity of the <s>guṇa</s>-s is unstable; but the naturalness of the <s>guṇa</s>-s has been stated to be the cause of activity; by this, in elements and senses, owing to the distinction between property and substrate, a threefold transformation is to be understood

children.text:
paramārthatas tv eka eva pariṇāmaḥ. dharmisvarūpamātro hi dharmo dharmivikriyaivaiṣā
            dharmadvārā prapañcyata iti. tatra dharmasya dharmiṇi vartamānasyaivādhvasv
            atītānāgatavartamāneṣu bhāvānyathātvaṃ bhavati na tu dravyānyathātvam. yathā
            suvarṇabhājanasya bhittvānyathākriyamāṇasya bhāvānyathātvaṃ bhavati na suvarṇānyathātvam
            iti.
children.translated_text: But in the highest truth, there is only one transformation; for property is merely the very form of the substrate, and this very alteration of property is what is elaborated through property; therein, of the property existing in the substrate itself, there is otherwiseness of being across the tracks of past, future, and present, but not otherwiseness of the substance; just as, for a gold vessel, when being broken and made otherwise, there is otherwiseness of being, but not otherwiseness of the gold

children.text:
apara āha --- dharmānabhyadhiko dharmī pūrvatattvānatikramāt. pūrvāparāvasthābhedam
            anupatitaḥ kauṭasthyenaiva parivarteta yady anvayī syād iti.
children.translated_text: Another says: the substrate is not superior to the properties, because the prior reality is not transgressed; if it were conjoined (anvayin), having not fallen into a difference of earlier and later states, it would revolve only by immobility (kauṭasthya), thus

children.text:
ayam adoṣaḥ. kasmāt. ekāntatānabhyupagamāt. tad etat trailokyaṃ vyakter apaiti
            nityatvapratiṣedhāt. apetam apy asti vināśapratiṣedhāt. saṃsargāc cāsya saukṣmyaṃ,
            saukṣmyāc cānupalabdhir iti.
children.translated_text: This is not a defect; why? Because exclusive absolutism is not admitted. Thus, this triad of worlds (<s>trailokya</s>) departs from manifestation due to the denial of eternality, yet even when it has departed it still exists, because annihilation is denied; and owing to its conjunction (with other factors) it is subtle, and because of subtlety there is non-perception—so it is

children.text:
lakṣaṇapariṇāmo dharmo+adhvasu vartamāno+atīto+atītalakṣaṇayukto+anāgatavartamānābhyāṃ
            lakṣaṇābhyām aviyuktaḥ. tathānāgato+anāgatalakṣaṇayukto vartamānātītābhyāṃ lakṣaṇābhyām
            aviyuktaḥ. tathā vartamāno vartamānalakṣaṇayukto+atītānāgatābhyāṃ lakṣaṇābhyām aviyukta
            iti. yathā puruṣa ekasyāṃ striyāṃ rakto na śeṣāsu virakto bhavatīti.
children.translated_text: The transformation of mark (<s>lakṣaṇa-pariṇāma</s>) is as follows: that which is past operates on the tracks (<s>adhvan</s>-s), being endowed with the past-mark and not dissociated from the marks of future and present; likewise that which is future, endowed with the future-mark, is not dissociated from the marks of present and past; likewise that which is present, endowed with the present-mark, is not dissociated from the marks of past and future. Just as a man (<s>puruṣa</s>) attached to one woman is not, for that reason, detached from the rest

children.text:
atra lakṣaṇapariṇāme sarvasya sarvalakṣaṇayogād adhvasaṃkaraḥ prāpnotīti parair doṣaś
            codyata iti. tasya parihāraḥ --- dharmāṇāṃ dharmatvam aprasādhyam. sati ca dharmatve
            lakṣaṇabhedo+api vācyo na vartamānasamaya evāsya dharmatvam. evaṃ hi na cittaṃ
            rāgadharmakaṃ syāt krodhakāle rāgasyāsamudācārād iti.
children.translated_text: Here, in the transformation of mark, because everything would be conjoined with every mark, a confusion of the tracks would ensue—thus a defect is alleged by others; its refutation is as follows: the being-a-property (property-hood) of properties (<s>dharmatva</s>) is not something to be established (by proof). And given that there is property-hood, one must also state a distinction of marks; nor is its property-hood only at the present moment. For otherwise, the mind (<s>citta</s>) would not be of the nature of passion (<s>rāga</s>) at the time of anger (<s>krodha</s>), since passion is not manifest then

children.text:
kiṃca trayāṇāṃ lakṣaṇānāṃ yugapad ekasyāṃ vyaktau nāsti saṃbhavaḥ. krameṇa tu
            svavyañjakāñjanasya bhāvo bhaved iti. uktaṃ ca rūpātiśayā vṛttyatiśayāś ca virudhyante,
            sāmānyāni tv atiśayaiḥ saha pravartante. tasmād asaṃkaraḥ yathā rāgasyaiva kvacit
            samudācāra iti na tadānīm anyatrābhāvaḥ, kiṃtu kevalaṃ sāmānyena samanvāgata ity asti
            tadā tatra tasya bhāvaḥ tathā lakṣaṇasyeti.
children.translated_text: Moreover, the simultaneous presence of the three marks in a single manifestation is not possible; rather, the being of that which has its own revealer arises in sequence. And it has been said: excellences of form and excellences of function are mutually opposed, whereas generalities do proceed together with excellences. Therefore there is no confusion: just as the occurrence of passion alone at some time does not entail the non-existence of other [properties] elsewhere at that time, but only that they are concomitant in a general way; therefore, there and then passion exists—so too the mark

children.text:
na dharmī tryadhvā dharmās tu tryadhvānas te lakṣitā alakṣitās tatra lakṣitās tāṃ tām
            avasthāṃ prāpnuvanto+anyatvena pratinirdiśyante+avasthāntarato na dravyāntarataḥ.
            yathaikā rekhā śatasthāne śataṃ daśasthāne daśaikā caikasthāne yathā caikatve+api strī
            mātā cocyate duhitā ca svasā ceti.
children.translated_text: The substrate is not three-tracked; rather, the properties are three-tracked. Those are marked and unmarked; among them, the marked, attaining this or that state, are designated as other, by difference of state and not by difference of substance. Just as one line is one hundred at the place of hundreds, ten at the place of tens, and one at the place of ones; and just as, though being one and the same, a woman is called mother, daughter, and sister

children.text:
avasthāpariṇāme kauṭasthyaprasaṅgadoṣaḥ kaiścid uktaḥ. katham. adhvano vyāpāreṇa
            vyavahitatvāt. yadā dharmaḥ svavyāpāraṃ na karoti tadānāgato yadā karoti tadā vartamāno
            yadā kṛtvā nivṛttas tadātīta ity evaṃ dharmadharmiṇor lakṣaṇānām avasthānāṃ ca
            kauṭasthyaṃ prāpnotīti parair doṣa ucyate.
children.translated_text: In the transformation of state (<s>avasthā-pariṇāma</s>), some have stated the defect of the consequence of immobility (<s>kauṭasthya</s>). How so? Because of separation by the operation of the track (<s>adhvan</s>). When a property does not perform its own operation, then it is future; when it performs it, then it is present; when, having performed it, it has ceased, then it is past—thus, a fixity of the marks of property and substrate and of states would result, say the others, as a defect

children.text:
nāsau doṣaḥ. kasmāt. guṇinityatve+api guṇānāṃ vimardavaicitryāt. yathā saṃsthānam
            ādimad dharmamātraṃ śabdādīnāṃ guṇānāṃ vināśyavināśinām evaṃ liṅgam ādimad dharmamātraṃ
            sattvādīnāṃ guṇānāṃ vināśyavināśinā tasmin vikārasaṃjñeti.
children.translated_text: That is not a defect; why? Because, even granting the permanence of the <s>guṇa</s>-s, there is diversity of their mutual interactions. Just as configuration and the like are mere properties of sound and so on—of qualities that are either perishable or imperishable—so too the indicator (mark) and the like are mere properties of the <s>guṇa</s>-s such as <s>sattva</s>, which are either perishable or imperishable; in regard to that, the term “modification” (<s>vikāra</s>) is applied

children.text:
tatredam udāharaṇaṃ mṛddharmī piṇḍākārād dharmād dharmāntaram upasaṃpadyamāno dharmataḥ
            pariṇamate ghaṭākāra iti. ghaṭākāro+anāgataṃ lakṣaṇaṃ hitvā vartamānalakṣaṇaṃ
            pratipadyata iti lakṣaṇataḥ pariṇamate. ghaṭo navapurāṇatāṃ pratikṣaṇam anubhavann
            avasthāpariṇāmaṃ pratipadyata iti. dharmiṇo+api dharmāntaram avasthā dharmasyāpi
            lakṣaṇāntaram avasthety eka eva dravyapariṇāmo bhedenopadarśita iti. evaṃ
            padārthāntareṣv api yojyam iti. ta ete dharmalakṣaṇāvasthāpariṇāmā dharmisvarūpam
            anatikrāntā ity eka eva pariṇāmaḥ sarvān amūn viśeṣān abhiplavate. atha ko+ayaṃ
            pariṇāmaḥ. avasthitasya dravyasya pūrvadharmanivṛttau dharmāntarotpattiḥ pariṇāma
            iti.
children.translated_text: Here is the example: the clay-substrate, proceeding from the property of lump-form to another property, transforms by way of property, becoming pot-form; the pot-form, having abandoned the future-mark and attained the present-mark, transforms by way of mark; the pot, experiencing newness and oldness at every moment, attains transformation of state. Thus, even for the substrate there is another property, a state; and for the property too another mark, a state—accordingly one and the same transformation of substance is displayed as distinct. This should be applied likewise to other categories. Therefore these transformations of property, mark, and state do not transgress the nature of the substrate; hence there is one single transformation that overflows all those distinctions. Now, what is this transformation? Of an abiding substance, when the prior property ceases and another property arises—that is called transformation
In that context —
The substrate (<s>dharmī</s>), which accompanies properties (<s>dharma</s>) designated as quieted, arisen, and indescribable (<s>śānta</s>, <s>udita</s>, <s>avyapadeśya</s>),

children.text:
yogyatāvacchinnā dharmiṇaḥ śaktir eva dharmaḥ. sa ca phalaprasavabhedānumita
            ekasyānyo+anyaś ca paridṛṣṭaḥ. tatra vartamānaḥ svavyāpāram anubhavan dharmī
            dharmāntarebhyaḥ śāntebhyaś cāvyapadeśyebhyaś ca bhidyate. yadā tu sāmānyena samanvāgato
            bhavati tadā dharmisvarūpamātratvāt ko+asau kena bhidyeta.
children.translated_text: A property (<s>dharma</s>) is nothing but the power (<s>śakti</s>) of the substrate (<s>dharmī</s>), delimited by suitability (yogyatā). And that [power], inferred from the distinctions of fruit and production, is observed as one in one case, and as another in another. Therein, the substrate, while experiencing its own operation in the present, is distinguished from other properties and from those that are quieted and from those that are indescribable; but when it is conjoined only generally, then, being nothing but the very nature of the substrate, what would that be, and by what would it be distinguished?

children.text:
tatra ye khalu dharmiṇo dharmāḥ śāntā uditā avyapadeśyāś ceti, tatra śāntā ye kṛtvā
            vyāpārānuparatāḥ savyāpārā uditās te cānāgatasya lakṣaṇasya samanantarā
            vartamānasyānantarā atītāḥ kimartham atītasyānantarā na bhavanti vartamānāḥ,
            pūrvapaścimatāyā abhāvāt. yathānāgatavartamānayoḥ pūrvapaścimatā naivam atītasya. tasmān
            nātītasyāsti samanantaraḥ tadanāgata eva samanantaro bhavati vartamānasyeti.
children.translated_text: As to the properties of the substrate, namely the quieted, the arisen, and the indescribable: among these, those that, having performed their operations, have ceased from activity are quieted, those with activity are arisen; and these [arisen] are immediately subsequent to the future-mark, and immediately prior to the present, and immediately past—why are the present not immediately prior to the past? Because there is no earlier–later relation between them; just as there is no earlier–later relation between future and present, not so for the past; therefore the past has no “immediately subsequent,” rather, the immediately subsequent to the present is only the not-yet-come (future),

children.text:
athāvyapadeśyāḥ ke sarvaṃ sarvātmakam iti. yatroktam --- jalabhūmyoḥ pāriṇāmikaṃ
            rasādivaiśvarūpyaṃ sthāvareṣu dṛṣṭam. tathā sthāvarāṇāṃ jaṅgameṣu jaṅgamānāṃ sthāvareṣv
            ity evaṃ jātyanucchedena sarvaṃ sarvātmakam iti.
children.translated_text: Now, which are the indescribable? [Those for which] “All is of the nature of all” (sarvaṃ sarvātmakam). As has been said: the varietal multiformity—of taste and the like—arising from transformation between water and earth is seen among immovables; likewise, of immovables in movables, and of movables in immovables—thus, by the non-termination of the genus, all is of the nature of all

children.text:
deśakālākāranimittāpabandhān na khalu samānakālam ātmanām abhivyaktir iti. ya eteṣv
            abhivyaktānabhivyakteṣu dharmeṣv anupātī sāmānyaviśeṣātmā so+anvayī dharmī. yasya tu
            dharmamātram evedaṃ niranvayaṃ tasya bhogābhāvaḥ. kasmāt, anyena vijñānena kṛtasya
            karmaṇo+anyat kathaṃ bhoktṛtvenādhikriyate. tatsmṛtyabhāvaś ca nānyadṛṣṭasya smaraṇam
            anyasyāstīti. vastupratyabhijñānāc ca sthito+anvayī dharmī yo dharmānyathātvam
            abhyupagataḥ pratyabhijñāyate tasmān nedaṃ dharmamātraṃ niranvayam iti.
children.translated_text: Because of the constraints of place, time, form, and occasion, verily there is not simultaneous manifestation of essences; that which, among properties manifested and unmanifested, accompanies them as a nature of the universal-and-particular (sāmānya-viśeṣa-ātmā), that, having pervasion (anvaya), is the substrate (<s>dharmī</s>). But for that of which there is merely property alone, without pervasion, there is absence of experience. Why? How would something other, as enjoyer, be authorized for an action performed by a cognition other? And the absence of its memory: there is remembrance of what has been seen, not of what is seen by another. And from the recognition of a real thing (vastu-pratyabhijñā), the abiding, pervading substrate is established; for that which admits the otherwiseness of property is recognized—therefore this is not mere property without pervasion
Difference of sequence is the cause of difference of transformation

children.text:
ekasya dharmiṇa eka eva pariṇāma iti prasakte kramānyatvaṃ pariṇāmānyatve hetur
            bhavatīti. tadyathā cūrṇamṛtpiṇḍamṛdghaṭamṛtkapālamṛtkaṇamṛd iti ca kramaḥ. yo yasya
            dharmasya samanantaro dharmaḥ sa tasya kramaḥ. piṇḍaḥ pracyavate ghaṭa upajāyata iti
            dharmapariṇāmakramaḥ. lakṣaṇapariṇāmakramo ghaṭasyānāgatabhāvād vartamānabhāvaḥ kramaḥ.
            tathā piṇḍasya vartamānabhāvād atītabhāvaḥ kramaḥ. nātītasyāsti kramaḥ. kasmāt.
            pūrvaparatāyāṃ satyāṃ samanantaratvaṃ, sā tu nāsty atītasya tasmād dvayor eva lakṣaṇayoḥ
            kramaḥ. tathāvasthāpariṇāmakramo+api ghaṭasyābhinavasya prānte purāṇatā dṛśyate. sā ca
            kṣaṇaparamparānupātinā krameṇābhivyajyamānā parāṃ vyaktim āpadyata iti.
            dharmalakṣaṇābhyāṃ ca viśiṣṭo+ayaṃ tṛtīyaḥ pariṇāma iti.
children.translated_text: When it might be maintained that there is only a single transformation of a single substrate, [we state:] difference of sequence is the cause of difference of transformation. For example: powder–clay, lump–clay, pot–clay, shard–clay, granule–clay—thus is the sequence. That property which is immediately subsequent to a given property is its sequence. “The lump perishes, the pot arises”—this is the sequence of transformation by property. The sequence of transformation by mark (<s>lakṣaṇa</s>) is: from the pot’s future-state to its present-state—this is the sequence; likewise, from the lump’s present-state to its past-state—this is the sequence. There is no sequence for the past. Why? Because immediacy (samanantaratva) obtains only where there is an earlier–later relation, and that does not obtain for the past; therefore sequence pertains only to the two marks. Likewise, the sequence of transformation by state (<s>avasthā</s>): for the pot, at the end of newness oldness is observed; and this, being manifested in a sequence that accompanies the succession of instants, attains a further manifestation. And this third transformation, distinguished by property and by mark, is this one [of state]

children.text:
ta ete kramā dharmadharmibhede sati pratilabdhasvarūpāḥ. dharmo+api dharmī bhavaty
            anyadharmasvarūpāpekṣayeti. yadā tu paramārthato dharmiṇy abhedopacāras taddvāreṇa sa
            evābhidhīyate dharmas tadāyam ekatvenaiva kramaḥ pratyavabhāsate.
children.translated_text: These sequences, given the distinction of property and substrate, have their nature established. And a property too becomes a substrate with respect to the nature of another property. But when, in the highest truth, there is a figurative ascription of non-difference within the substrate, then by that very doorway, that very thing is spoken of as a property; then this sequence appears as just one by oneness

children.text:
cittasya dvaye dharmā paridṛṣṭāś cāparidṛṣṭāś ca. tatra pratyayātmakāḥ paridṛṣṭā
            vastumātrātmakā aparidṛṣṭāḥ. te ca saptaiva bhavanty anumānena
            prāpitavastumātrasadbhāvāḥ.
children.translated_text: In the mind (<s>citta</s>) there are two [classes of] properties: observed and unobserved. Among these, those of the nature of cognitive content (<s>pratyaya</s>) are observed, those of the nature of mere real thing (vastu-mātra) are unobserved. And these are only seven in number—the existence of mere real things having been established by inference
The impressions (<s>saṃskāra</s>) of the property of restraint (<s>nirodha</s>) are the transformation; and then life

children.text: ceṣṭā śaktiś ca cittasya dharmā darśanavarjitāḥ //
children.translated_text: Effort and power are properties of the mind (<s>citta</s>), devoid of observability,
—so it is said.

children.text:
ato yogina upāttasarvasādhanasya bubhutsitārthapratipattaye saṃyamasya viṣaya
            upakṣipyate ---
children.translated_text: Therefore, for the yogin who has acquired all the means, in order to attain the desired object of knowledge, the scope of <s>saṃyama</s> is set forth—
From <s>saṃyama</s> on the triad of transformations, knowledge of the past and the future [arises]

children.text:
dharmalakṣaṇāvasthāpariṇāmeṣu saṃyamād yogināṃ bhavaty atītānāgatajñānam.
            dhāraṇādhyānasamādhitrayam ekatra saṃyama uktaḥ. tena pariṇāmatrayaṃ sākṣātkriyamāṇam
            atītānāgatajñānaṃ teṣu saṃpādayati.
children.translated_text: By <s>saṃyama</s> on the transformations of property (<s>dharma</s>), mark (<s>lakṣaṇa</s>), and state (<s>avasthā</s>), there arises for yogins knowledge of the past and the future. The triad of <s>dhāraṇā</s>, <s>dhyāna</s>, and <s>samādhi</s> is called <s>saṃyama</s> upon a single object; through that, as the triad of transformations is directly realized, knowledge of past and future is produced in regard to them,

Because of the mutual superimposition of sound, meaning, and cognition, there is a confusion; from <s>saṃyama</s> on their differentiation, [there arises] knowledge of the cries (utterances) of all beings

children.text:
tatra vāgvarṇeṣv evārthavatī. śrotraṃ ca dhvanipariṇāmamātraviṣayam. padaṃ punar
            nādānusaṃhārabuddhinirgrāhyam iti. varṇā ekasamayāsaṃbhavitvāt
            parasparaniranugrahātmānas te padam asaṃspṛśyānupasthāpyāvirbhūtās tirobhūtāś ceti
            pratyekam apadasvarūpā ucyante.
children.translated_text: Therein, only in the speech-sounds does there reside meaningfulness; and the ear has as its object merely the transformation of sound (i.e., vibration). A word (pada), however, is graspable only by a cognition that gathers up and integrates the sequence of sounds—thus. Since phonemes (varṇa) cannot occur simultaneously, having the nature of not mutually assisting one another, each one—without touching upon or presenting the word—appears, then disappears; therefore, taken individually, they are said to be non-word in nature,

children.text:
varṇaḥ punar ekaikaḥ padātmā sarvābhidhānaśaktipracitaḥ sahakārivarṇāntarapratiyogitvād
            vaiśvarūpyam ivāpannaḥ pūrvaś cottareṇottaraś ca pūrveṇa viśeṣe+avasthāpita ity evaṃ
            bahavo varṇāḥ kramānurodhino+arthasaṃketenāvacchinnā iyanta ete
            sarvābhidhānaśaktiparivṛtā gakāraukāravisarjanīyāḥ sāsnādimantam arthaṃ dyotayantīti.
children.translated_text: Yet each single phoneme, being of the nature of the word, is filled with the entire capacity to denote; by opposition to the assisting other phonemes, it seems as though it had manifold forms, and the prior is determined by the subsequent and the subsequent by the prior in respect of particularization—thus, many phonemes, following the order, delimited by the convention regarding meaning, being endowed with the full capacities of denotation, the ga, the u, and the visarga (ḥ), indicate a meaning that has features such as a muzzle (sāsnā), etc.

children.text:
tad eteṣām arthasaṃketenāvacchinnānām upasaṃhṛtadhvanikramāṇāṃ ya eko buddhinirbhāsas
            tatpadaṃ vācakaṃ vācyasya saṃketyate. tad ekaṃ padam ekabuddhiviṣaya ekaprayatnākṣiptam
            abhāgam akramam avarṇaṃ bauddham antyavarṇapratyayavyāpāropasthāpitaṃ paratra
            pratipipādayiṣayā varṇair evābhidhīyamānaiḥ śrūyamāṇaiś ca śrotṛbhir
            anādivāgvyavahāravāsanānuviddhayā lokabuddhyā siddhavatsaṃpratipattyā pratīyate.
children.translated_text: Now, for these whose sequences of sounds have been gathered up and delimited by the convention regarding meaning, there is a single cognition-appearance; that is the word (pada), the designator of the designated. That single word, pertaining to a single cognition and impelled by a single effort, being partless, non-sequential, non-phonemic, mental, and presented by the operation of the cognition of the final phoneme, is, for the purpose of bringing about understanding in another place, expressed precisely by those very phonemes that are uttered and heard; and by the worldly mind, infused with the beginningless impressions of linguistic usage, it is apprehended with an understanding like that of something already established (i.e., commonly agreed),

children.text:
tasya saṃketabuddhitaḥ pravibhāga etāvatām evaṃjātīyako+anusaṃhāra ekasyārthasya vācaka
            iti. saṃketas tu padapadārthayor itaretarādhyāsarūpaḥ smṛtyātmako yo+ayaṃ śabdaḥ so+ayam
            artho yo+ayam arthaḥ so+ayaṃ śabda iti. evam itaretarādhyāsarūpaḥ saṃketo bhavatīti.
            evam ete śabdārthapratyayā itaretarādhyāsāt saṃkīrṇā gaur iti śabdo gaur ity artho gaur
            iti jñānam. ya eṣāṃ pravibhāgajñaḥ sa sarvavit.
children.translated_text: From the cognition of convention, its differentiation is thus: a gathering-up of just these [phonemes], of this kind, is the designator of a single meaning. And convention is of the form of mutual superimposition between word and word-meaning, being of the nature of memory: “this is that word, this is that meaning; this meaning is this word, this word is this meaning”—in this way convention comes to be of the nature of mutual superimposition. Thus, these—sound, meaning, and cognition—are confounded through mutual superimposition: ‘gauḥ’ is the word; ‘gauḥ’ is the meaning; ‘gauḥ’ is the cognition. Whoever knows their differentiation is omniscient with respect to them,

children.text:
sarvapadeṣu cāsti vākyaśaktivṛkṣa ity ukte+astīti gamyate. na sattāṃ padārtho
            vyabhicaratīti. tathā na hy asādhanā kriyāstīti.
children.translated_text: And in all words there exists what is called the tree of sentence-power—thus, it is inferred that it exists. The reality of a word-meaning does not deviate [from that], likewise, actions do not occur without instruments,

children.text:
tathā ca pacatīty ukte sarvakārakāṇām ākṣepo niyamārtho+anuvādaḥ kartṛkaraṇakarmaṇāṃ
            caitrāgnitaṇḍulānām iti. dṛṣṭaṃ ca vākyārthe padaracanaṃ śrotriyaś chando+adhīte, jīvati
            prāṇān dhārayati. tatra vākye padārthābhivyaktis tataḥ padaṃ pravibhajya vyākaraṇīyaṃ
            kriyāvācakaṃ vā kārakavācakaṃ vā. anyathā bhavaty aśvo+ajāpaya ity evamādiṣu
            nāmākhyātasārūpyād anirjñātaṃ kathaṃ kriyāyāṃ kārake vā vyākriyeteti.
children.translated_text: Accordingly, when one says “he cooks,” there is the enjoinment (ākṣepa), the force of restriction, and the reiteration regarding all the <s>kāraka</s>-s: agent, instrument, and object—namely of <s>caitra</s>, fire, and rice-grains. And it is observed that there is word-arrangement with respect to a sentence-meaning: “the Vedic scholar studies <s>chandas</s>,” “he lives,” “he sustains breaths.” There, in the sentence, there is manifestation of word-meanings; therefore a word should be analyzed, after being differentiated, as either denoting an action or denoting a <s>kāraka</s>. Otherwise, in cases like “the horse goats” (aśvo ajāpaya) and the like, due to the similarity of noun and verb, being not ascertained, how would it be parsed as denoting an action or a <s>kāraka</s>?

children.text:
teṣāṃ śabdārthapratyayānāṃ pravibhāgaḥ. tadyathā śvetate prāsāda iti kriyārthaḥ, śvetaḥ
            prāsāda iti kārakārthaḥ śabdaḥ, kriyākārakātmā tadarthaḥ pratyayaś ca. kasmāt so+ayam
            ity abhisaṃbandhād ekākāra eva pratyayaḥ saṃketa iti.
children.translated_text: Thus there is a differentiation of sound, meaning, and cognition. For example: “he whitens the palace” (śvetate prāsāda) is an action-meaning; “white is the palace” (śvetaḥ prāsāda) is a word (śabda) with a <s>kāraka</s>-meaning; and the cognition (pratyaya) is of the nature of action-and-<s>kāraka</s> whose meaning is that. Why so? Because, through the relation ‘this is that,’ the cognition is of a single form—this is convention

children.text:
yas tu śveto+arthaḥ sa śabdapratyayayor ālambanībhūtaḥ. sa hi svābhir avasthābhir
            vikriyamāṇo na śabdasahagato na buddhisahagataḥ. evaṃ śabda evaṃ pratyayo
            netaretarasahagata ity anyathā śabdo+anyathārtho+anyathā pratyaya iti vibhāgaḥ. evaṃ
            tatpravibhāgasaṃyamād yoginaḥ sarvabhūtarutajñānaṃ saṃpadyata iti.
children.translated_text: But that which is the white-meaning—this becomes the support for word and cognition; for, undergoing modification in its own states, it is not conjoined with the word, nor is it conjoined with the cognition; thus, ‘this is the word, this is the cognition, and they are not mutually conjoined’—otherwise it would be ‘the word is otherwise, the meaning otherwise, the cognition otherwise’: this is the differentiation; thus, by <s>saṃyama</s> (the combined practice of <s>dhāraṇā</s>, <s>dhyāna</s>, and <s>samādhi</s>) upon that very differentiation, there accrues to the yogin knowledge of the utterances of all beings
From the direct realization of impressions (<s>saṃskāra</s>), knowledge of previous births

children.text:
dvaye khalv amī saṃskārāḥ smṛtikleśahetavo vāsanārūpā vipākahetavo dharmādharmarūpāḥ.
            te pūrvabhavābhisaṃskṛtāḥ pariṇāmaceṣṭānirodhaśaktijīvanadharmavad aparidṛṣṭāś
            cittadharmāḥ. teṣu saṃyamaḥ saṃskārasākṣātkriyāyai samarthaḥ. na ca
            deśakālanimittānubhavair vinā teṣām asti sākṣātkaraṇam. tad itthaṃ saṃskārasākṣātkaraṇāt
            pūrvajātijñānam utpadyate yoginaḥ. paratrāpy evam eva saṃskārasākṣātkaraṇāt
            parajātisaṃvedanam.
children.translated_text: Indeed, these impressions are twofold: as causes of memory and affliction (<s>kleśa</s>), they are of the nature of latent dispositions (<s>vāsanā</s>); as causes of fruition, they are of the nature of merit and demerit (<s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>); being formed in prior existences, they are properties of the mind (<s>citta-dharma</s>) not directly perceived, like the powers of transformation, effort, restraint, vitality (<s>jīvana</s>), and the like; upon these, <s>saṃyama</s> is capable of bringing about the direct realization of impressions; and there is no direct realization of them without experiences conditioned by place, time, and occasion; therefore, in this way, from the direct realization of impressions, knowledge of previous births arises for the yogin; and similarly elsewhere too, from the direct realization of impressions, there is cognition of others’ births

children.text:
atredam ākhyānaṃ śrūyate --- bhagavato jaigīṣavyasya saṃskārasākṣātkaraṇād daśasu
            mahāsargeṣu janmapariṇāmakramam anupaśyato vivekajaṃ jñānaṃ prādurabhūt. atha bhagavān
            āvaṭyas tanudharas tam uvāca --- daśasu mahāsargeṣu bhavyatvād anabhibhūtabuddhisattvena
            tvayā narakatiryaggarbhasaṃbhavaṃ duḥkhaṃ saṃpaśyatā devamanuṣyeṣu punaḥ punar
            utpadyamānena sukhaduḥkhayoḥ kim adhikam upalabdham iti. bhagavantam āvaṭyaṃ jaigīṣavya
            uvāca. daśasu mahāsargeṣu bhavyatvād anabhibhūtabuddhisattvena mayā narakatiryagbhavaṃ
            duḥkhaṃ saṃpaśyatā devamanuṣyeṣu punaḥ punar utpadyamānena yat kiṃcid anubhūtaṃ tat
            sarvaṃ duḥkham eva pratyavaimi. bhagavān āvaṭya uvāca. yad idam āyuṣmataḥ
            pradhānavaśitvam anuttamaṃ ca saṃtoṣasukhaṃ kim idam api duḥkhapakṣe nikṣiptam iti.
            bhavagāñ jaigīṣavya uvāca --- viṣayasukhāpekṣayaivedam anuttamaṃ saṃtoṣasukham uktam.
            kaivalyasukhāpekṣayā duḥkham eva. buddhisattvasyāyaṃ dharmas triguṇas triguṇaś ca
            pratyayo heyapakṣe nyasta iti. duḥkharūpas tṛṣṇātantuḥ. tṛṣṇāduḥkhasaṃtāpāpagamāt tu
            prasannam abādhaṃ sarvānukūlaṃ sukham idam uktam iti.
children.translated_text: Here a tale is heard: for the Blessed <s>Jaigīṣavya</s>, from the direct realization of impressions, while beholding in sequence the order of birth-transformation across the ten great creations, there arose knowledge born of discriminative discernment; then the Blessed <s>Āvaṭya</s>, being slender-bodied, said to him: ‘Across the ten great creations, since you are capable and, with a mind of <s>sattva</s> not overcome, seeing the suffering consisting of womb-birth in hells and among animals, and being born again and again among gods and humans—what have you ascertained to be predominant between pleasure and pain?’ The Blessed one, <s>Jaigīṣavya</s>, said to the Blessed <s>Āvaṭya</s>: ‘Across the ten great creations, since I, being capable and with a mind of <s>sattva</s> not overcome, seeing the suffering of hell and animal existence, and being born again and again among gods and humans, whatever has been experienced, all that I indeed apprehend as suffering alone.’ The Blessed <s>Āvaṭya</s> said: ‘This sovereignty over the <s>Pradhāna</s> (primordial matter) of the venerable one, and the unsurpassed happiness of contentment—are even these placed on the side of suffering?’ The Blessed <s>Jaigīṣavya</s> said: ‘This unsurpassed happiness of contentment was stated only in comparison to sense-pleasures; in comparison to the happiness of <s>kaivalya</s> (isolation/liberation), it is indeed suffering; this is the property of the luminosity of intellect (<s>buddhi-sattva</s>): it is three-<s>guṇa</s>-ed, and the cognition too is three-<s>guṇa</s>-ed, and is placed on the side to-be-abandoned; the strand of craving is of the form of suffering; but from the cessation of the torment of craving-and-suffering, this happiness, serene, unobstructed, universally favorable, is declared’
Knowledge of another’s mind from [the object] of cognition

children.text: pratyaye saṃyamāt pratyayasya sākṣātkaraṇāt tataḥ paracittajñānam.
children.translated_text: From <s>saṃyama</s> on the cognitive content (<s>pratyaya</s>), from the direct realization of the cognitive content, then knowledge of another’s mind
And that is not with its support, because that is not its object

children.text:
raktaṃ pratyayaṃ jānāty amuṣminn ālambane raktam iti na jānāti. parapratyayasya yad
            ālambanaṃ tad yogicittena nālambanīkṛtaṃ parapratyayamātraṃ tu yogicittasyālambanībhūtam
            iti.
children.translated_text: He knows the reddened cognition, but regarding that support he does not know ‘reddened’; that which is the support of another’s cognition is not made into a support by the yogin’s mind, whereas only the other’s cognition itself becomes the support for the yogin’s mind
From <s>saṃyama</s> on body-form, when there is the arresting of the power of that which is to be grasped by the eye, through the non-conjunction with the light of the eye there is invisibility

children.text:
kāyasya rūpe saṃyamād rūpasya yā grāhyā śaktis tāṃ pratiṣṭabhnāti. grāhyaśaktistambhe
            sati cakṣuṣprakāśāsaṃprayoge+antardhānam utpadyate yoginaḥ. etena śabdādyantardhānam
            uktaṃ veditavyam.
children.translated_text: From <s>saṃyama</s> on the form of the body, he arrests the power by which form is graspable; when the graspable-power is arrested, through the non-conjunction with the light of the eye, invisibility arises for the yogin; by this it should be understood that the disappearance of sound and the rest has been stated

children.text: sopakramaṃ nirupakramaṃ ca karma tatsaṃyamād aparāntajñānam ariṣṭebhyo vā
children.translated_text: Karma is with-commencement and without-commencement; from <s>saṃyama</s> on that, knowledge of the end of another’s life, or from portents (<s>ariṣṭa</s>)

children.text:
āyurvipākaṃ karma dvividhaṃ sopakramaṃ nirupakramaṃ ca. tatra yathārdraṃ vastraṃ
            vitānitaṃ laghīyasā kālena śuṣyet tathā sopakramam. yathā ca tad eva saṃpiṇḍitaṃ cireṇa
            saṃśuṣyed evaṃ nirupakramam. yathā vāgniḥ śuṣke kakṣe mukto vātena samantato yuktaḥ
            kṣepīyasā kālena dahet tathā sopakramam. yathā vā sa evāgnis tṛṇarāśau kramaśo 'vayaveṣu
            nyastaś cireṇa dahet tathā nirupakramam. tadaikabhavikam āyuṣkaraṃ karma dvividhaṃ
            sopakramaṃ nirupakramaṃ ca. tatsaṃyamād aparāntasya prāyaṇasya jñānam.
children.translated_text: Karma that yields lifespan-result is twofold: with-commencement and without-commencement. Therein, just as a wet cloth, having been spread out, would dry in a shorter time, so is the with-commencement; and just as that very cloth, when tightly wrung together, would dry only after a long time, so is the without-commencement. And just as fire, set in a dry thicket and joined on all sides with wind, would burn in a shorter time, so is the with-commencement; and just as that same fire, placed successively upon the parts in a heap of grass, would burn only after a long time, so is the without-commencement. Therefore the karma that produces lifespan in a single birth is twofold, with-commencement and without-commencement; from <s>saṃyama</s> (the combined practice of <s>dhāraṇā</s>, <s>dhyāna</s>, and <s>samādhi</s>) on that, there is knowledge of the end of another’s departure (death)

children.text:
ariṣṭebhyo veti trividham ariṣṭam ādhyātmikam ādhibhautikam ādhidaivikaṃ ceti.
            tatrādhyātmikaṃ ghoṣaṃ svadehe pihitakarṇo na śṛṇoti, jyotir vā netre+avaṣṭabdhe na
            paśyati. tathādhibhautikaṃ yamapuruṣān paśyati, pitṝn atītān akasmāt paśyati.
            tathādhidaivikaṃ svargam akasmāt siddhān vā paśyati. viparītaṃ vā sarvam iti anena vā
            jānāty aparāntam upasthitam iti.
children.translated_text: Or from portents (<s>ariṣṭa</s>): the <s>ariṣṭa</s> are threefold—pertaining to the self (<s>ādhyātmika</s>), pertaining to beings/elements (<s>ādhibhautika</s>), and pertaining to deities (<s>ādhidaivika</s>). There, the <s>ādhyātmika</s> is: one does not hear a sound in one’s own body when the ear is covered, or one does not see light in the eye though it is steady; likewise, the <s>ādhibhautika</s>: one sees the messengers of <s>Yama</s>, one sees ancestors (<s>pitṛ</s>-s) who have passed away, unexpectedly; likewise, the <s>ādhidaivika</s>: one sees heaven unexpectedly, or <s>siddha</s>-s; or all is inverted—by this he knows that the end (death) has approached
The powers in friendliness and the like

children.text:
maitrī karuṇā muditeti tisro bhāvanās tatra bhūteṣu sukhiteṣu maitrīṃ bhāvayitvā
            maitrībalaṃ labhate. duḥkhiteṣu karuṇāṃ bhāvayitvā karuṇābalaṃ labhate. puṇyaśīleṣu
            muditāṃ bhāvayitvā muditābalaṃ labhate. bhāvanātaḥ samādhir yaḥ sa saṃyamas tato balāny
            avandhyavīryāṇi jāyante. pāpaśīleṣūpekṣā na tu bhāvanā. tataś ca tasyāṃ nāsti samādhir
            ity ato na balam upekṣātas tatra saṃyamābhāvād iti.
children.translated_text: There are three cultivations: friendliness (<s>maitrī</s>), compassion (<s>karuṇā</s>), and sympathetic joy (<s>mudita</s>). Therein, having cultivated <s>maitrī</s> toward beings who are happy, one obtains the power of <s>maitrī</s>; having cultivated <s>karuṇā</s> toward those who are suffering, one obtains the power of <s>karuṇā</s>; having cultivated <s>mudita</s> toward the virtuous, one obtains the power of <s>mudita</s>. From cultivation there is <s>samādhi</s>; that is <s>saṃyama</s>; from that, powers arise, unfailing in energy. Toward those of sinful disposition there is equanimity (<s>upekṣā</s>), but not cultivation; therefore therein there is no <s>samādhi</s>; hence there is no power from <s>upekṣā</s> there, due to the absence of <s>saṃyama</s>
Among the powers, those such as the strength of an elephant and the like

children.text:
hastibale saṃyamād dhastibalo bhavati. vainateyabale saṃyamād vainateyabalo bhavati.
            vāyubale saṃyamād vāyubalo bhavatīty evamādi.
children.translated_text: From <s>saṃyama</s> on the strength of an elephant, he attains the strength of an elephant; from <s>saṃyama</s> on the strength of <s>Vainateya</s> (the divine eagle), he attains the strength of <s>Vainateya</s>; from <s>saṃyama</s> on the strength of wind, he attains the strength of wind—thus and the like
From the depositing of illumination by activity, knowledge of the subtle, the obstructed (concealed), and the distant

children.text:
jyotiṣmatī pravṛttir uktā manasas tasyā ya ālokas taṃ yogī sūkṣme vā vyavahite vā
            viprakṛṣṭe vārthe vinyasya tam artham adhigacchati.
children.translated_text: The luminous operation (<s>jyotiṣmatī pravṛtti</s>) of the mind (<s>manas</s>) has been spoken of; the light of that, the yogin, by depositing upon an object—whether subtle, or obstructed, or distant—attains that object
Knowledge of the worlds from <s>saṃyama</s> on the sun

children.text:
tatprastāraḥ sapta lokāḥ. tatrāvīceḥ prabhṛti merupṛṣṭhaṃ yāvad ity evaṃ bhūrlokaḥ.
            merupṛṣṭhād ārabhya --- ādhruvād grahanakṣatratārāvicitro+antarikṣalokaḥ. tataḥ paraḥ
            svarlokaḥ pañcavidho māhendras tṛtīyo lokaḥ. caturthaḥ prājāpatyo maharlokaḥ. trividho
            brāhmaḥ tadyathā --- janalokas tapolokaḥ satyaloka iti.
children.translated_text: Its expansion is the seven worlds. Therein, beginning from <s>Avīci</s> up to the summit of <s>Meru</s>—thus is the <s>Bhū</s>-world. Beginning from the summit of <s>Meru</s>, the intermediate space (<s>antarikṣa</s>)-world is variegated by <s>Dhruva</s> and below, by planets, lunar mansions, and stars. Beyond that is the heaven (<s>svar</s>-world), fivefold; the third world is the <s>Māhendra</s>. The fourth, belonging to <s>Prajāpati</s>, is the great world, <s>Mahas</s>. The threefold is the <s>Brāhma</s>; namely: the world of <s>Jana</s>, the world of <s>Tapas</s>, the world of <s>Satya</s>

children.text: brāhmas tribhūmiko loka prājāpatyas tato mahān /
children.translated_text: The <s>Brāhma</s> world is three-territoried; thereafter the <s>Prajāpatya</s>, then the great; and the <s>Māhendra</s> is said to be the heaven (<s>svar</s>); in the sky the stars, on earth the creatures

children.text: māhendraś ca svar ity ukto divi tārā bhuvi prajāḥ //

children.translated_text: —thus is the verse of summary
Thus, the summary-verse

children.text:
tatrāvīcer upary upari niviṣṭāḥ ṣaṇmahānarakabhūmayo
            ghanasalilānalānilākāśatamaḥpratiṣṭhā
            mahākālāmbarīṣarauravamahārauravakālasūtrāndhatāmisrāḥ. yatra
            svakarmopārjitaduḥkhavedanāḥ prāṇinaḥ kaṣṭam āyur dīrgham ākṣipya jāyante. tato
            mahātalarasātalātalasutalavitalatalātalapātālākhyāni sapta pātālāni. bhūmir iyam aṣṭamī
            saptadvīpā vasumatī, yasyāḥ sumerur madhye parvatarājaḥ kāñcanaḥ. tasya
            rājatavaidūryasphaṭikahemamaṇimayāni śṛṅgāṇi. tatra vaidūryaprabhānurāgān
            nīlotpalapatraśyāmo nabhaso dakṣiṇo bhāgaḥ, śvetaḥ pūrvaḥ, svacchaḥ paścimaḥ,
            kuraṇṭakābha uttaraḥ. dakṣiṇapārśve cāsya jambūr yato+ayaṃ jambūdvīpaḥ. tasya
            sūryapracārād rātriṃdivaṃ lagnam iva vartate. tasya nīlaśvetaśṛṅgavanta udīcīnās trayaḥ
            parvatā dvisāhasrāyāmāḥ. tadantareṣu trīṇi varṣāṇi nava nava yojanasāhasrāṇi ramaṇakaṃ
            hiraṇmayam uttarāḥ kurava iti. niṣadhahemakūṭahimaśailā dakṣiṇato dvisāhasrāyāmāḥ.
            tadantareṣu trīṇi varṣāṇi nava nava yojanasāhasrāṇi harivarṣaṃ kiṃpuruṣaṃ bhāratam iti.
            sumeroḥ prācīnā bhadrāśvamālyavatsīmānaḥ pratīcīnāḥ ketumālā gandhamādanasīmānaḥ. madhye
            varṣamilāvṛtam. tad etad yojanaśatasāhasraṃ sumeror diśidiśi tadardhena vyūḍham.
children.translated_text: There, above Avīci, one above another, are situated the six great hell-realms, whose foundations are compact water, fire, wind, space, and darkness—namely <s>Mahākālāmbarīṣa</s>, <s>Raurava</s>, <s>Mahāraurava</s>, <s>Kālasūtra</s>, and <s>Andhatāmisra</s>; in which living beings, experiencing the pains earned by their own karma, having a wretched and long life, are cast and are born; then, the seven <s>Pātāla</s> regions named <s>Mahātala</s>, <s>Rasātala</s>, <s>Atala</s>, <s>Sutala</s>, <s>Vitalatala</s>, <s>Atala</s> (variant), and <s>Pātāla</s>; this earth is the eighth, the seven-continent <s>Vasumatī</s>, in whose center is <s>Sumeru</s>, the golden king of mountains; its peaks are of silver, beryl, crystal, gold, and gem; there, because of the affection of the luster of beryl, the southern portion of the sky is dark like the petal of a blue lotus, the eastern is white, the western is clear, the northern is like a kurantaka (coral-like) hue; and on its southern side is the <s>Jambu</s> tree, whence this is the <s>Jambūdvīpa</s>; by its (the <s>Jambu</s> tree’s) spreading of sunlight, night and day proceed as though fixed to the ascendant; to its north are three mountains with blue and white peaks, two-thousand yojanas in extent; in the intervals between them are three regions, each nine thousand yojanas, namely <s>Ramaṇaka</s>, <s>Hiraṇmaya</s>, and the <s>Uttarāḥ Kuravaḥ</s>; to the south are <s>Niṣadha</s>, <s>Hemakūṭa</s>, and <s>Himāśaila</s>, two-thousand yojanas (in extent); in the intervals between them are three regions, each nine thousand yojanas, namely <s>Harivarṣa</s>, <s>Kiṃpuruṣa</s>, and <s>Bhārata</s>; east of <s>Sumeru</s> are the boundaries of <s>Bhadrāśva</s> and <s>Mālyavat</s>, to the west the boundaries of <s>Ketumālā</s> and <s>Gandhamādana</s>; in the middle is the region encircled by the mountain-range; all this is a hundred thousand yojanas, laid out around <s>Sumeru</s> in each of the quarters, and in the intermediate directions arranged to the extent of half that

children.text:
sa khalv ayaṃ śatasāhasrāyāmo jambūdvīpas tato dviguṇena lavaṇodadhinā valayākṛtinā
            veṣṭitaḥ. tataś ca dviguṇā dviguṇāḥ śākakuśakrauñcaśālmalagomedha(plakṣa) puṣkaradvīpāḥ,
            samudrāś ca sarṣaparāśikalpāḥ savicitraśailāvataṃsā
            ikṣurasasurāsarpirdadhimaṇḍakṣīrasvādūdakāḥ. sapta samudrapariveṣṭitā valayākṛtayo
            lokālokaparvataparivārāḥ pañcāśad yojanakoṭiparisaṃkhyātāḥ. tad etat sarvaṃ
            supratiṣṭhitasaṃsthānamaṇḍamadhye vyūḍham. aṇḍaṃ ca pradhānasyāṇur avayavo yathākāśe
            khadyota iti.
children.translated_text: And indeed this <s>Jambūdvīpa</s> is one hundred thousand yojanas across, and is encircled by the salt ocean, in the form of a ring, measuring twice that; and thereafter, each twice the previous, are the continents <s>Śāka</s>, <s>Kuśa</s>, <s>Krauñca</s>, <s>Śālmalā</s>, <s>Gomedha</s> (<s>Plakṣa</s>), and <s>Puṣkara</s>; and the oceans, proportioned like mustard and sesame (i.e., successively broader), adorned with variegated mountains, having the tastes of sugarcane-juice, wine, ghee, curd-whey, milk, and sweet water; encircled by seven oceans, in ring shapes, furnished with the <s>Loka-āloka</s> mountain, they are counted as fifty crore yojanas; and all this is arranged within the well-established central part of the cosmic egg; and the egg is a subtle part of <s>Pradhāna</s> (primordial matter)—like a firefly in the sky, so it is said

children.text:
tatra pātāle jaladhau parvateṣv eteṣu devanikāyā
            asuragandharvakiṃnarakiṃpuruṣayakṣarākṣasabhūtapretapiśācāpasmārakāpsarobrahmarākṣasakūṣmāṇḍavināyakāḥ
            prativasanti. sarveṣu dvīpeṣu puṇyātmāno devamanuṣyāḥ.
children.translated_text: There, in <s>Pātāla</s>, in the ocean, in the mountains, in these places, the classes of gods reside—<s>Asura</s>, <s>Gandharva</s>, <s>Kiṃnara</s>, <s>Kiṃpuruṣa</s>, <s>Yakṣa</s>, <s>Rākṣasa</s>, <s>Bhūta</s>, <s>Preta</s>, <s>Piśāca</s>, <s>Apasmāraka</s>, <s>Apsaras</s>, <s>Brahmarākṣasa</s>, <s>Kūṣmāṇḍa</s>, and <s>Vināyaka</s>; on all the continents dwell virtuous ones—gods and humans

children.text:
sumerus tridaśānām udyānabhūmiḥ tatra miśravanaṃ nandanaṃ caitrarathaṃ sumānasam ity
            udyānāni. sudharmā devasabhā sudarśanaṃ puram. vaijayantaḥ prāsādaḥ.
            grahanakṣatratārakās tu dhruve nibaddhā vāyuvikṣepaniyamenopalakṣitapracārāḥ sumeror
            upary upari saṃniviṣṭā divi viparivartante.
children.translated_text: <s>Sumeru</s> is the garden-ground of the Thirty-three (<s>Tridaśa</s>); there are the groves <s>Miśravaṇa</s>, <s>Nandana</s>, <s>Caitraratha</s>, and <s>Sumānasa</s>, such are the parks; <s>Sudharmā</s> is the divine assembly-hall, <s>Sudarśana</s> the city; <s>Vaijayanta</s> the palace; the planets, lunar mansions, and stars are fastened to <s>Dhruva</s>, their courses observed by the regulation of the casting by wind, and, positioned one above another over <s>Sumeru</s>, they revolve in the sky

children.text:
māhendranivāsinaḥ ṣaḍdevanikāyāḥ --- tridaśā agniṣvāttā yāmyās tuṣitā
            aparinirmitavaśavartinaḥ parinirmitavaśavartinaś ceti. sarve saṃkalpasiddhā
            aṇimādyaiśvaryopapannāḥ kalpāyuṣo vṛndārakāḥ kāmabhogina aupapādikadehā uttamānukūlābhir
            apsarobhiḥ kṛtaparicārāḥ.
children.translated_text: The six classes of gods dwelling in the <s>Māhendra</s> (heaven) are—the <s>Tridaśa</s>, the <s>Agniṣvātta</s>, the <s>Yāmya</s>, the <s>Tuṣita</s>, the <s>Aparinirmitavaśavartin</s>, and the <s>Parinirmitavaśavartin</s>; all accomplish by mere resolve, endowed with the lordly powers beginning with <s>aṇimā</s> (minuteness), having the lifespan of an aeon, attendant youths, enjoyers of sense-pleasures, with spontaneously produced bodies, and waited upon by <s>Apsaras</s> of supremely agreeable forms

children.text:
mahati loke prājāpatye pañcavidho devanikāyaḥ --- kumudā ṛbhavaḥ pratardanā añjanābhāḥ
            pracitābhā iti. ete mahābhūtavaśino dhyānāhārāḥ kalpasahasrāyuṣaḥ. prathame brahmaṇo
            janaloke caturvidho devanikāyo brahmapurohitā brahmakāyikā brahmamahākāyikā amarā iti.
            te bhūtendriyavaśino dviguṇadviguṇottarāyuñaḥ.
children.translated_text: In the great world of <s>Prajāpati</s>, there is a fivefold class of gods—<s>Kumuda</s>, <s>Ṛbhava</s>, <s>Pratardana</s>, <s>Añjanābhā</s>, and <s>Pracitābhā</s>; these hold sway over the great elements (<s>mahābhūta</s>), take meditation as their food, and have lifespans of a thousand aeons. In the first, in the world of <s>Brahmā</s> called <s>Jana</s>, there is a fourfold class of gods—<s>Brahmapurohita</s>-s, <s>Brahmakāyika</s>-s, <s>Brahmamahākāyika</s>-s, and the <s>Amara</s>-s; they hold sway over the elements-and-senses (<s>bhūta</s>-<s>indriya</s>) and have lifespans that are successively doubled upon being doubled

children.text:
dvitīye tapasi loke trividho devanikāyaḥ --- ābhāsvarā mahābhāsvarāḥ satyamahābhāsvarā
            iti. te bhūtendriyaprakṛtivaśino dviguṇadviguṇottarāyuṣaḥ sarve dhyānāhārā ūrdhvaretasa
            ūrdhvam apratihatajñānā adharabhūmiṣv anāvṛtajñānaviṣayāḥ. tṛtīye brahmaṇaḥ satyaloke
            catvāro devanikāyā akṛtabhavananyāsāḥ svapratiṣṭhā uparyuparisthitāḥ pradhānavaśino
            yāvat sargāyuṣaḥ.
children.translated_text: In the second, in the world of <s>Tapas</s>, there is a threefold class of gods—<s>Ābhāsvara</s>, <s>Mahābhāsvara</s>, and <s>Satyamahābhāsvara</s>; they hold sway over elements, senses, and <s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature), all have lifespans successively doubled upon being doubled, subsist on meditation, are upward-viriled (<s>ūrdhvaretas</s>), unimpeded in knowledge upwards, and in the lower levels their fields of knowledge are not veiled. In the third, in the world of <s>Brahmā</s> called <s>Satya</s>, there are four classes of gods, who have not undertaken the establishment of abodes, having their own foundation, situated higher and higher, holding sway over <s>Pradhāna</s> (primordial matter), with lifespans that last as long as a creation-cycle

children.text:
tatrācyutāḥ savitarkadhyānasukhāḥ, śuddhanivāsāḥ savicāradhyānasukhāḥ, satyābhā
            ānandamātradhyānasukhāḥ, saṃjñāsaṃjñinaś cāsmitāmātradhyānasukhāḥ. te+api
            trailokyamadhye pratitiṣṭhanti. ta ete sapta lokāḥ sarva eva brahmalokāḥ.
            videhaprakṛtilayās tu mokṣapade vartanta iti na lokamadhye nyastā iti. etad yoginā
            sākṣātkaraṇīyaṃ sūryadvāre saṃyamaṃ kṛtvā, tato+anyatrāpi evaṃ tāvad abhyased yāvad idaṃ
            sarvaṃ dṛṣṭam iti.
children.translated_text: There, the <s>Acyuta</s>-s enjoy the bliss of <s>savitaraka-dhyāna</s> (discernment-with-thought meditation); the <s>Śuddhanivāsa</s>-s enjoy the bliss of <s>savicāra-dhyāna</s> (reflection-with-inquiry meditation); the <s>Satyābhā</s>-s enjoy the bliss of meditation consisting solely of bliss (<s>ānandamātra-dhyāna</s>); and the <s>Saṃjñāsaṃjñin</s>-s enjoy the bliss of meditation consisting solely of <s>asmitā</s> (I-am-ness). These too stand established in the midst of the three worlds. These are the seven worlds, all indeed the worlds of <s>Brahmā</s>. But those of disembodiedness and dissolution-into-<s>Prakṛti</s> (<s>videha</s> and <s>prakṛtilaya</s>) operate on the path of liberation, therefore they are not placed within the midst of the worlds. This should be directly realized by the yogin, having performed <s>saṃyama</s> on the gate of the sun; thereafter, elsewhere too, let him so practice until this entire [cosmos] has been seen
From [<s>saṃyama</s> on] the moon, knowledge of the array of stars

children.text: candre saṃyamaṃ kṛtvā tārāṇāṃ vyūhaṃ vijānīyāt.
children.translated_text: Having performed <s>saṃyama</s> on the moon, one should discern the configuration of the stars
From [<s>saṃyama</s> on] <s>Dhruva</s> (the Pole Star), knowledge of their motion

children.text:
tato dhruve saṃyamaṃ kṛtvā tārāṇāṃ gatiṃ vijānīyāt ūrdhvavimāneṣu kṛtasaṃyamas tāni
            vijānīyāt.
children.translated_text: Then, having performed <s>saṃyama</s> on <s>Dhruva</s>, one should discern the movement of the stars; having performed <s>saṃyama</s> on the aerial vehicles above, one should discern those
From [<s>saṃyama</s> on] the navel wheel, knowledge of the arrangement of the body

children.text:
nābhicakre saṃyamaṃ kṛtvā kāyavyūhaṃ vijānīyāt vātapittaśleṣmāṇas trayo doṣāḥ. dhātavaḥ
            sapta tvaglohitamāṃsasnāyvasthimajjāśukrāṇi pūrvaṃ pūrvam eṣāṃ bāhyam ity eṣa
            vinyāsaḥ.
children.translated_text: Having performed <s>saṃyama</s> on the navel wheel, one should discern the arrangement of the body: the three humors are wind, bile, and phlegm (<s>vāta</s>, <s>pitta</s>, <s>śleṣman</s>); the constituents are seven—skin, blood, flesh, sinews, bone, marrow, and semen—each preceding of these is external to the subsequent: this is the layout
In the throat-pit, the cessation of hunger and thirst

children.text:
jihvāyā adhastāt tantus tantor adhastāt kaṇṭhas tato+adhastāt kūpas tatra saṃyamāt
            kṣutpipāse na bādhete.
children.translated_text: Below the tongue is a tendon, below the tendon the throat, and below that the pit; by <s>saṃyama</s> there, hunger and thirst do not afflict
In the <s>Kūrma-nāḍī</s>, steadiness

children.text:
kūpād adha urasi kūrmākārā nāḍī, tasyāṃ kṛtasaṃyamaḥ sthirapadaṃ labhate yathā sarpo
            godhā veti.
children.translated_text: Below the pit, in the chest, is a channel shaped like a tortoise, the <s>nāḍī</s> called <s>Kūrma</s>; performing <s>saṃyama</s> on that, one attains a firm posture, as a serpent or a monitor-lizard [would be steady]
In the light at the crown, the sight of <s>Siddha</s>-s

children.text:
śiraḥkapāle+antaś chidraṃ prabhāsvaraṃ jyotis tatra saṃyamaṃ kṛtvā siddhānāṃ
            dyāvāpṛthivyor antarālacāriṇāṃ darśanam.
children.translated_text: Within the skull-cap there is an opening, a radiant light; having performed <s>saṃyama</s> there, there is the seeing of the <s>Siddha</s>-s moving in the space between heaven and earth
Or by [the knowledge called] <s>Prātibha</s>, everything

children.text:
prātibhaṃ nāma tārakaṃ tadvivekajasya jñānasya pūrvarūpam. yathodaye prabhā
            bhāskarasya. tena vā sarvam eva jānāti yogī prātibhasya jñānasyotpattāv iti.
children.translated_text: <s>Prātibha</s> is named the polestar; it is the preliminary form of knowledge born of discriminative discernment, just as at sunrise the radiance of the sun. By that, the yogin knows indeed everything, upon the arising of <s>Prātibha</s>-knowledge
In the heart, awareness of mind (<s>citta</s>)

children.text:
yad idam asmin brahmapure daharaṃ puṇḍarīkaṃ veśma tatra vijñānaṃ tasmin saṃyamāc
            cittasaṃvit.
children.translated_text: That which here, in this city of <s>Brahman</s>, is the small lotus-like abode—there is cognition; from <s>saṃyama</s> on that, there is awareness of the mind (<s>citta-saṃvit</s>)

children.text:
sattvapuruṣayor atyantāsaṃkīrṇayoḥ pratyayāviśeṣo bhogaḥ parārthāt svārthasaṃyamāt
              puruṣajñānam
children.translated_text: Experience is the non-difference of cognitive presentations for <s>sattva</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s>, which are absolutely non-intermingled; because [<s>sattva</s>] is for the sake of another (<s>parārtha</s>), from <s>saṃyama</s> for one’s own sake (<s>svārtha</s>), knowledge of <s>Puruṣa</s>

children.text:
buddhisattvaṃ prakhyāśīlaṃ samānasattvopanibandhane rajastamasī vaśīkṛtya
            sattvapuruṣānyatāpratyayena pariṇatam. tasmāc ca sattvāt pariṇāmino+atyantavidharmā
            viśuddho+anyaś citimātrarūpaḥ puruṣaḥ. tayor atyantāsaṃkīrṇayoḥ pratyayāviśeṣo bhogaḥ
            puruṣasya darśitaviṣayatvāt sa bhogapratyayaḥ sattvasya parārthatvād dṛśyaḥ.
children.translated_text: The luminosity of intellect (<s>buddhi-sattva</s>) has the character of manifestness; when bound together with a substratum of like-<s>sattva</s>, having subdued rajas and tamas, it is transformed with the cognition of the otherness of <s>sattva</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s>. And from that <s>sattva</s>, which is subject to transformation, the <s>Puruṣa</s>, absolutely of a different property, pure, other, of the nature of mere awareness, [is established]. For these two, absolutely non-intermingled, experience is the non-difference of cognitive presentations, because for <s>Puruṣa</s> it has the status of the object made manifest; that experience-cognition is of <s>sattva</s>, which, being for the sake of another, is the seen

children.text:
yas tu tasmād viśiṣṭaś citimātrarūpo+anyaḥ pauruṣeyaḥ pratyayas tatra saṃyamāt
            puruṣaviṣayā prajñā jāyate. na ca puruṣapratyayena buddhisattvātmanā puruṣo dṛśyate
            puruṣa eva taṃ pratyayaṃ svātmāvalambanaṃ paśyati tathā hy uktam --- ``

children.translated_text: By what, indeed, would one know the Knower,

But that other, distinct from that, of the form of mere awareness, the puruṣa-based cognition—by <s>saṃyama</s> on that, insight concerning <s>Puruṣa</s> arises; and <s>Puruṣa</s> is not seen by a puruṣa-cognition whose nature is the luminosity of intellect (<s>buddhi-sattva</s>)—rather, <s>Puruṣa</s> himself beholds that cognition, which has his own self as its support, for thus it is said—“
Then arise reports of <s>Prātibha</s> (intuitive insight), clairaudience, clair-tactile perception, visionary seeing, and exquisite taste,

children.text:
prātibhāt sūkṣmavyavahitaviprakṛṣṭātītānāgatajñānam. śrāvaṇād divyaśabdaśravaṇam.
            vedanād divyasparśādhigamaḥ. ādarśād divyarūpasaṃvit āsvādād divyarasasaṃvit vārtāto
            divyagandhavijñānam ity etāni nityaṃ jāyante.
children.translated_text: From <s>Prātibha</s>, knowledge of the subtle, the interveningly remote, the far-off, the past, and the future; from clairaudience, the hearing of divine sounds; from tactile-cognition, attainment of divine touch; from visionary-seeing, knowledge of divine forms; from exquisite taste, knowledge of divine flavors; from report, knowledge of divine scents—these arise continually
These are impediments in <s>samādhi</s>, and perfections (<s>siddhi</s>-s) in emergence (from absorption)

children.text:
te prātibhādayaḥ samāhitacittasyotpadyamānā upasargās taddarśanapratyanīkatvāt
            vyutthitacittasyotpadyamānāḥ siddhayaḥ.
children.translated_text: These, beginning with <s>Prātibha</s>, arising for one whose mind (<s>citta</s>) is collected in <s>samādhi</s>, are impediments, because they are opposed to the vision (of truth); arising for one whose mind is emergent, they are <s>siddhi</s>-s
From the loosening of the cause of bondage and from knowledge of the course (movement) of the mind, there is entry of the mind into another’s body

children.text:
lolībhūtasya manaso+apratiṣṭhasya śarīre karmāśayavaśād bandhaḥ pratiṣṭhety arthaḥ
            tasya karmaṇo bandhakāraṇasya śaithilyaṃ samādhibalād bhavati. pracārasaṃvedanaṃ ca
            cittasya samādhijam eva karmabandhakṣayāt svacittasya pracārasaṃvedanāc ca yogī cittaṃ
            svaśarīrān niṣkṛṣya śarīrāntareṣu nikṣipati. nikṣiptaṃ cittaṃ cendriyāṇy anu patanti.
            yathā madhukararājānaṃ makṣikā utpatantam anūtpatanti niviśamānam anu niviśante
            tathendriyāṇi paraśarīrāveśe cittam anu vidhīyanta iti.
children.translated_text: The binding—namely the establishment of the mind, which has become unsteady and ungrounded in the body—occurs by the power of the deposit of karma; the slackening of that, the cause of bondage—of that karma—takes place through the power of <s>samādhi</s>. And the cognition of the mind’s movement is itself born of <s>samādhi</s>; through the destruction of karmic bondage and through awareness of the movement of one’s own mind, the yogin draws his mind out from his own body and deposits it into other bodies; and when the mind has been deposited, the senses follow in its wake. Just as bees follow their king-bee—when he takes off, they take off after him; when he settles, they settle after him—so, in entering another’s body, the senses are directed after the mind
From the mastery of <s>Udāna</s> (the upward-breath), non-contact with water, mud, thorns, and the like, and also ascension (at death)

children.text:
samastendriyavṛttiḥ prāṇādilakṣaṇā jīvanaṃ, tasya kriyā pañcatayī prāṇo
            mukhanāsikāgatir āhṛdayavṛttiḥ. samaṃ nayanāt samānaś cānābhivṛttiḥ. apanayanād apāna
            āpādatalavṛttiḥ unnayanād udāna āśirovṛttiḥ vyāpī vyāna iti. eṣāṃ pradhānaṃ prāṇaḥ
            udānajayāj jalapaṅkakaṇṭakādiṣv asaṅga utkrāntiś ca prāyaṇakāle bhavati tāṃ vaśitvena
            pratipadyate.
