Then, because of the infinity of knowledge, from which all coverings and stains are removed, the knowable is small

children.text:
sarvaiḥ kleśakarmāvaraṇair vimuktasya jñānasyānantyaṃ bhavati. āvarakeṇa
            tamasābhibhūtam āvṛtam anantaṃ jñānasattvaṃ kvacid eva rajasā pravartitam udghāṭitaṃ
            grahaṇasamarthaṃ bhavati. tatra yadā sarvair āvaraṇamalair apagataṃ bhavati tadā bhavaty
            asyānantyam. jñānasyānantyāj jñeyam alpaṃ saṃpadyate yathākāśe khadyotaḥ. yatredam uktam
            ---
children.translated_text: For knowledge, freed from all coverings of afflictions and karma, there is infinitude; the existent of knowledge (<s>jñāna-sattva</s>), infinite, overpowered and covered by the covering darkness, being at some time set in motion by <s>rajas</s>, opened up, becomes capable of apprehension; there, when it becomes freed from all covering-stains, then it attains infinitude; and because of the infinitude of knowledge, the knowable becomes little—like a firefly in the sky; as this has been said—

children.text: andho maṇim avidhyat tam anaṅgulir āvayat /
children.translated_text: The blind man did not pierce the jewel, the fingerless one set it in motion toward him,
the neckless one wore it, the tongueless one offered it worship,”
—so it is said
Then, for those whose purpose is accomplished, there is the completion of the sequence of transformations of the <s>guṇa</s>-s

children.text:
tasya dharmameghasyodayāt kṛtārthānāṃ guṇānāṃ pariṇāmakramaḥ parisamāpyate na hi
            kṛtabhogāpavargāḥ parisamāptakramāḥ kṣaṇam apy avasthātum utsahante.
children.translated_text: From the rise of that cloud-of-dharma, the sequence of transformations of the <s>guṇa</s>-s—whose purpose is accomplished—is brought to completion; for those whose enjoyment and liberation (<s>bhoga</s> and <s>apavarga</s>) have been accomplished, whose sequence is brought to an end, do not endure even for a moment
Now, what is this sequence, called “sequence”—
Sequence is that which is apprehended at the other end (termination) of a transformation, with a moment as its counterpart

children.text:
kṣaṇānantaryātmā pariṇāmasyāparāntenāvasānena gṛhyate kramaḥ na hy ananubhūtakramakṣaṇā
            purāṇatā vastrasyānte bhavati nityeṣu ca kramo dṛṣṭaḥ.
children.translated_text: Sequence, whose nature is the unbroken succession of moments, is grasped by the conclusion (other-end) of a transformation; for there is no oldness at the end of a cloth for moments of sequence not experienced, and in what is eternal sequence is observed

children.text:
dvayī ceyaṃ nityatā kūṭasthanityatā pariṇāminityatā ca. tatra kūṭasthanityatā
            puruṣasya. pariṇāminityatā guṇānām. yasmin pariṇamyamāne tattvaṃ na vihanyate tan nityam
            ubhayasya ca tattvānabhighātān nityatvam. tatra guṇadharmeṣu buddhyādiṣu
            pariṇāmāparāntanirgrāhyaḥ kramo labdhaparyavasāno nityeṣu dharmiṣu guṇeṣv
            alabdhaparyavasānaḥ. kūṭasthanityeṣu svarūpamātrapratiṣṭheṣu muktapuruṣeṣu svarūpāstitā
            krameṇaivānubhūyata iti tatrāpy alabdhaparyavasānaḥ śabdapṛṣṭhenāstikriyām upādāya
            kalpita iti.
children.translated_text: And this eternality is twofold: rock-steady eternality and transforming eternality; there, rock-steady eternality belongs to the <s>Puruṣa</s>, transforming eternality to the <s>guṇa</s>-s; that in which, while transforming, the reality is not subverted—that is eternal; and, because the realities of both are not struck down, there is eternality; there, in the properties of the <s>guṇa</s>-s—such as intellect (<s>buddhi</s>) and the rest—the sequence, apprehended at the termination of a transformation, has obtained its conclusion, but in the eternal substrates, the <s>guṇa</s>-s, it has not obtained a conclusion; in those who are rock-steadily eternal, established only in their own nature—the liberated <s>Puruṣa</s>-s—the existence of their own nature is experienced indeed only in sequence, therefore there too it has not obtained a conclusion; this (view), taking up the affirmation “there is” from the back of the word (i.e., from verbal usage), is a construction (a conceptual posit)

children.text:
athāsya saṃsārasya sthityā gatyā ca guṇeṣu vartamānasyāsti kramasamāptir na veti.
            avacanīyam etat katham asti praśna ekāntavacanīyaḥ sarvo jāto mariṣyatīti oṃ bhoḥ iti.
children.translated_text: Now, as to this saṃsāra—does there exist a completion of sequence in the <s>guṇa</s>-s in which it abides by its persistence and movement, or not? This is inexpressible; how could it be?—the question “Is it?” is absolutely answerable: “All who are born will die”—om, sir

children.text:
atha sarvo mṛtvā janiṣyata iti vibhajyavacanīyam etat. pratyuditakhyātiḥ kṣīṇatṛṣṇaḥ
            kuśalo na janiṣyata itaras tu janiṣyate. tathā manuṣyajātiḥ śreyasī na vā śreyasīty evaṃ
            paripṛṣṭe vibhajya vacanīyaḥ praśnaḥ paśūn adhikṛtya śreyasī devān ṛṣīṃś cādhikṛtya
            neti. ayaṃ tv avacanīyaḥ praśnaḥ saṃsāro+ayam antavān athānanta iti. kuśalasyāsti
            saṃsārakramasamāptir netarasyeti anyatarāvadhāraṇe doṣaḥ tasmād vyākaraṇīya evāyaṃ
            praśna iti.
children.translated_text: Now, “All who have died will be born”—this ought to be stated by distinguishing cases. The one in whom discriminative cognition (<s>khāti</s> [scil. <s>pratyudita-khyāti</s>]) has arisen and craving is exhausted, the skillful one, will not be born; but the other will be born. Likewise, regarding the human kind: “Is it better (more conducive to <s>śreyas</s>) or not better?”—when asked thus, the question ought to be answered by distinguishing cases: in regard to beasts it is not better, in regard to the gods and <s>ṛṣi</s>-s it is better. But this question is unstateable: “Is this <s>saṃsāra</s> finite or infinite?” Determining on either side—“for the skillful one there is completion of the sequence of <s>saṃsāra</s>, not for the other”—there is a defect; therefore, indeed this question ought to be declined (not taken up)
At the completion of the sequence governing the jurisdiction of the <s>guṇa</s>-s, <s>kaivalya</s> was stated; its own nature is to be ascertained—

children.text: puruṣārthaśūnyānāṃ guṇānāṃ pratiprasavaḥ kaivalyaṃ svarūpapratiṣṭhā vā citiśaktir iti
children.translated_text: The involution (<s>pratiprasava</s>) of the <s>guṇa</s>-s that are devoid of purpose for the <s>Puruṣa</s> is <s>kaivalya</s>, or the establishment in one’s own form; that is, the power of consciousness (<s>citi-śakti</s>)

children.text:
kṛtabhogāpavargāṇāṃ puruṣārthaśūnyānāṃ yaḥ pratiprasavaḥ kāryakāraṇātmakānāṃ guṇānāṃ
            tat kaivalyaṃ, svarūpapratiṣṭhā punar buddhisattvānabhisaṃbandhāt puruṣasya citiśaktir
            eva kevalā, tasyāḥ sadā tathaivāvasthānaṃ kaivalyam iti.
children.translated_text: For those <s>guṇa</s>-s whose enjoyment and liberation (<s>bhoga</s> and <s>apavarga</s>) have been accomplished and which are devoid of purpose for the <s>Puruṣa</s>, that involution of the <s>guṇa</s>-s whose nature is effect-and-cause—that is <s>kaivalya</s>; but establishment in one’s own form, due to the non-connection of the <s>Puruṣa</s> with the <s>buddhi</s>-<s>sattva</s>, is the power of consciousness (<s>citi-śakti</s>) alone, isolated; the perpetual abiding of that just so is <s>kaivalya</s>

children.text:
iti śrīpātañjale sāṃkhyapravacane yogaśāstre vyāsabhāṣye kaivalyapādaś caturthaḥ
            4.
children.translated_text: Thus ends, in the Yoga treatise, the exposition of <s>Sāṃkhya</s> by the venerable <s>Patañjali</s>, in <s>Vyāsa</s>’s commentary, the fourth chapter, the Kaivalya Section—4
